title: Executors, futures, and virtual threads — Module Quiz
description: Course assessment: A service makes several independent blocking lookups.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: Which workload is a good candidate for virtual threads?

options.text: One CPU-bound calculation needing faster arithmetic
A request to increase database capacity automatically

questions.explanation: Virtual threads improve scalability for waiting tasks.

questions.prompt: Do virtual threads enlarge the database connection pool?
questions.explanation: External resource capacity remains a separate limit.

questions.prompt: What does Future.get(timeout, unit) time out?

options.text: The caller’s wait for a result

questions.explanation: The task may continue unless cancelled or otherwise bounded.

questions.prompt: Who should close a task executor?

options.text: The garbage collector on a schedule

questions.explanation: Explicit ownership prevents leaked work and resources.

questions.prompt: Should virtual threads usually be pooled to reuse a fixed set of them?
questions.explanation: Use one virtual thread per task and bound scarce resources separately.

questions.prompt: Does cancel(true) guarantee an immediate task stop?

questions.explanation: Two tasks receive independent virtual threads; execution order is unspecified. get waits as needed; output order is determined by concatenation, not task completion order. The executor closes after its tasks finish.
